newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore sees healthy economic growth in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Singapore sees healthy economic growth in 1997.

text.p: Singapore said on Tuesday it expected respectable economic growth in 1997, although its forecast was more conservative than those of private economists. The Ministry of Trade and Industry said in a statement the Singapore 5.0 to 7.0 percent in 1997, a figure it has been using for some time and unchanged on Tuesday despite signs that a slight decline in growth might have reached its bottom.
Most economists predict 1997 growth of slightly more than 7.0 percent.
The government figures for 1996 announced on Tuesday showed the new year began from a strong launching pad.

The ministry said December growth was stronger than expected and lifted economic expansion for the fourth quarter to 5.8 percent and for the whole of 1996 to 7.0 percent, a figure that had been announced earlier.
It said recent indications from the electronics industry, which accounts for some 60 percent of Singapore's non-oil exports, suggested improvements ahead, such as stronger demand for computers.
The financial and business services sector helped the 1996 figures, growing 10 percent last year compared to 7.6 percent in the previous year.
That contrasted sharply with a steep drop in manufacturing growth, from 10 percent in 1995 to just 3.4 percent last year, a fall resulting from a sluggish electronics sector.
The transport and communications sector, which includes Singapore's bustling port, was also relatively sluggish. Growth dropped from 10.8 percent in 1995 to 7.6 percent last year.

The construction sector was relatively strong in 1996, but in a sign the government wanted to keep up the momentum, the ministry said on Tuesday Singapore would award Singapore $11.2 billion (US$7.9 billion) in public sector construction contracts in 1997.
That is up from S$10.5 billion in 1996, when the construction sector grew by 13.7 percent, up from just 8.5 percent in 1995. (US$1=S$1.42)
